title: Per-participant trajectories with a mean trajectory: grouping, ordering and missing scores
source_relation: original construction on the grouping/ordering failure family; shuffled input rows and missing scores added
difficulty_hypothesis: Without an explicit group aesthetic all rows form one path; geom_path (unlike geom_line) joins points in row order so shuffled data zig-zags; averaging with missing scores treated as zero biases the mean line; and the mean line is easily left visually indistinguishable.

mcp_relevance.rationale: Grouping and drawing order are core ggplot2 semantics; the answer does not rest on a package fact or version.
mcp_relevance.information_need: The group aesthetic and the difference between geom_line and geom_path ordering.
alternative_solution_paths: geom_line(aes(group = subject)) plus a precomputed mean line

blockers: ceiling effect likely for strong baselines: calibration must confirm

pinned_evidence.oracle: plain-R per-subject (week, score) sequences and weekly means; compared as sets of sequences from ggplot_build layer data, independent of group numbering
